title: pySpark within AWS Lambda container
question:
I want to create a lambda function using pyspark to ingest a small amount of data into a datalake in order to avoid the (costly) overhead of glue jobs. I created a custom docker image. Even though the image works locally, I fail to execute it within aws.

I made sure, all environmental variables from my local .env file are available and the container is not running out of memory. It might be noteworthy, that i locally build on an arm64 and the aws image is built with github actions on amd64.

Currently, the application loads a small csv file from S3 and shows it. Running the container locally results in the following logs. I am looking for support/suggestions, how I need to adjust my approach.

answer:
I found the answer for the problem:

Within the spark-class file, a process substitution is used which is not allowed within AWS Lambda. The solution is adjusting the spark-class and write the result of build_command into a temporary file and then pass the content to the while loop, where the main execution command CMD is built.

There are a couple of alternate spark-class files in various git repos, but they dont work on amazon linux 2023 any more - at least not in the python 3.13 image. I can send my edited spark-class file if anyone is interested.
